companies.name: Epiroc
notes: Profit metric changed from 'Adj. operating profit, EBIT' (previous run) to 'EBITA' so Epiroc compares like-for-like with competitors on the EBITA basis. Epiroc's EBITA is unadjusted: per its definitions table, EBITA = operating profit (EBIT) plus amortization and impairment of intangible assets; it therefore includes items affecting comparability (e.g. 2024Q3 EBITA 3 896 includes a +554 revaluation gain on ASI Mining shares, with the 346 impairment of acquired intangibles added back).

Adjusted EBITA (higher in the priority list) was not used: the Group interim reports print no adjusted-EBITA figure (only text mentions about the Stanley Infrastructure acquisition), the key-figures file shows 'Adjusted EBITA' only from 2023Q1 with no published definition, so it can neither be sourced nor derived for 2021-2022.

Reported EBITA: 2024Q1-2026Q3 from each quarter's own interim report (p.3 Financial overview); 2023Q1-Q4 from the 2024 interim reports' prior-year comparatives (EBITA was introduced in the Q1 2024 report); 2022Q1-Q4 from Epiroc's own historical key-figures file (Epiroc Key Figures Q3 2026, sheet 'Key figures', row '* EBITA'), which reports EBITA quarterly from 2022Q1.

Derived quarters 2021Q1-2021Q4 (profit_derived=true): EBITA = Operating profit, EBIT (printed p.3 of that quarter's interim report) + amortization and impairment of intangible assets (Epiroc Key Figures Q3 2026, sheet 'Cash flow', row 55 'Intangible assets'; the interim reports print only total depreciation, amortization and impairment). EBIT values in the reports equal the key-figures file ('APMs calculated' row 10).

Formula proof on overlap quarters where Epiroc reports EBITA (EBIT + intangible D&A vs reported EBITA): 2022Q1: 2631 + 124 = 2755 vs reported 2755 (+0.00%); 2022Q2: 2381 + 132 = 2513 vs reported 2513 (+0.00%); 2022Q3: 2900 + 140 = 3040 vs reported 3040 (+0.00%); 2022Q4: 3235 + 232 = 3467 vs reported 3467 (+0.00%); 2023Q1: 3161 + 213 = 3374 vs reported 3374 (+0.00%); 2023Q2: 3413 + 192 = 3605 vs reported 3605 (+0.00%); 2023Q3: 3260 + 273 = 3533 vs reported 3533 (+0.00%); 2023Q4: 3349 + 217 = 3566 vs reported 3566 (+0.00%); 2024Q1: 2760 + 216 = 2976 vs reported 2976 (+0.00%). All within 0.5% (max deviation on all overlap quarters 2022Q1-2026Q3: 0.05%).

No restatement of Group revenue/EBIT found for 2021-2026 (restatements of 2022/2023 relate only to business-area splits and to orders received, which are not used here). Values are MSEK as reported; reported_margin_pct is Epiroc's printed EBITA margin (one decimal) and null for derived quarters.

source.title: Epiroc AB Interim Report January – September 2026 (Q3 2026)
source.locator: p.3 'Financial overview' table (repeated p.5), Q3 2026 column: Revenues 16 775; EBITA 3 686; EBITA margin 22.0%

points: Orders received rose 15% to MSEK 17 467 (12% organic), driven by strong mining demand, with mining customers at 83% of Group orders and large orders of MSEK 790 including a MSEK 610 MMG order for the Khoemacau copper mine in Botswana.
Operating profit rose 22% to MSEK 3 411 and the adjusted operating margin improved to 20.4% (19.0) on higher volumes and efficiency actions, while EBITA reached MSEK 3 686, a 22.0% margin.

Epiroc expects mining demand to remain high and infrastructure demand to remain stable in the near term, while operating cash flow fell to MSEK 1 438 (2 476) as more inventory was tied up after strong equipment orders.

companies.name: Sandvik
companies.segment: Mining and Rock Solutions business area (reported as 'Mining' since the Q4 2025 report)
notes: Reports in SEK, calendar fiscal year; fx_rate_to_sek = 1.0 for all quarters.

The business area Sandvik Mining and Rock Solutions (SMR) has been reported under the name 'Mining' since the Q4 2025 report (the 2026 structure has four business areas: Mining, Rock Processing, Machining, Intelligent Manufacturing). The Mining history is identical to the SMR history (e.g. 2024Q1 revenue 14,312 / adj. EBITA 2,605 in both the Q1 2024 and Q3 2026 reports), so this is a rename and not a restatement.

Restatement used: SMR adjusted EBITA for the 2021 quarters was restated in the Q1 2022 report, when Sandvik Materials Technology/Alleima moved to discontinued operations (e.g. Q4 2021 2,782 originally, 2,825 restated; revenues unchanged). The restated figures, which are also in Sandvik's current financial-data Excel, are used.

Backfill 2021Q1–2025Q4 comes from Sandvik's quarterly financial-data Excel (2026 Q3 edition). Every quarter was checked against the business-area tables in the interim reports, and all revenue, adjusted EBITA and margin values match the reports to the rounded MSEK/0.1 pp. The 2026 quarters are sourced directly from the 2026 interim reports.
Mining figures are as reported, including bolt-on acquisitions from their consolidation dates; no restatement of Mining history has been published for the 2026 structure.

companies.name: Caterpillar
notes: Profit metric: Caterpillar reports no EBITA, adjusted EBITA, adjusted EBIT or EBIT at segment level; Resource Industries 'Segment Profit' is the highest metric in the priority list that is available, so it is used for every quarter. It is the company's segment measure: restructuring costs, corporate costs, timing and methodology differences are excluded and sit in the reconciliation to consolidated profit.
Revenue = Resource Industries 'Total Sales' including inter-segment sales; Caterpillar's printed 'Segment Profit Margin' is computed on this figure.

Restatement (recast, used): Form 8-K of 2026-03-26 (Ex. 99.1) recast 2024Q1–2025Q4 Resource Industries sales and segment profit for the Rail division move from Power & Energy into Resource Industries (effective 2026-01-01) and for responsibility transfers first disclosed in the Q3 2025 10-Q: wear and maintenance components moved in from the All Other Segment, while electronics/control systems and autonomy/automation R&D moved out to the All Other Segment. 2024Q1–2024Q4 and 2025Q4 come from that 8-K, which prints no margin, so reported_margin_pct is null. 2025Q1–Q3 come from the recast prior-year columns of the 2026 earnings releases, which are identical to the 8-K and do print margins.

Structural break: Caterpillar has published no Rail recast for 2021–2023, so 2021Q1–2023Q4 are on the pre-2026 segment basis (excluding Rail, before the 2025 responsibility transfers) and are not like-for-like with 2024Q1 onward. On the recast basis, 2024Q1 sales are 4,015 versus 3,193 originally reported.

Restatement (recast, used): 2021 segment information was recast in 2022 for a methodology change in how intersegment sales and segment profit from technology products are assigned (Q1 2022 Form 10-Q, note 16). 2021 quarters therefore use the prior-year columns of the 2022 earnings releases (e.g. 2021Q1 2,178 / 312 versus 2,216 / 328 originally). 2022 and 2023 quarters use the prior-year columns of the 2023 and 2024 releases, which equal the original figures.
All quarters are single calendar quarters as printed; no YTD derivation was needed. Nothing is derived (profit_derived=false throughout).
Next report date: Caterpillar has said Q4 2026 results and the 2027 outlook come in January 2027, but had not announced an exact date as of 2026-11-10, so next_report_date is null.
FX: Riksbank quarterly average SEK per 1 USD (series SEKUSDPMI).

points: Resource Industries total sales rose 15% to $4.615 billion in Q3 2026, driven mainly by $478 million of higher sales volume and $96 million of favorable price realization.

Segment profit rose 14% to $622 million, but the margin slipped to 13.5% from 13.6% as $208 million of unfavorable manufacturing costs, mainly higher material costs including tariffs, offset volume and price gains.
Caterpillar said Heavy Construction and Quarry & Aggregates sales rose mainly on changes in dealer inventories, while Rail sales fell on lower international locomotive deliveries.

companies.name: Komatsu
companies.fiscal_year_note: Komatsu's fiscal year starts 1 April (FY2026 = Apr 2026–Mar 2027). Fiscal quarters are mapped to the calendar quarter they end in: FY Q1 (Apr–Jun) = calendar Q2 of the same year, FY Q2 (Jul–Sep) = Q3, FY Q3 (Oct–Dec) = Q4, FY Q4 (Jan–Mar) = Q1 of the following calendar year. So 2021Q1 = FY2020 Q4 (labelled 'FY20/4Q' by Komatsu) and 2026Q3 = FY2026 Q2 ('FY26/2Q').
notes: Profit metric: Komatsu reports no EBITA, EBIT or adjusted EBIT for its segments, so CMU 'Segment profit' is used for every quarter. It is net sales minus cost of sales and SG&A and excludes 'other operating income (expenses)'. The printed margin is 'Segment profit ratio'.
Revenue = CMU segment sales including inter-segment sales (the bracketed 'sales to outside customers' figures are not used); Komatsu's segment profit ratio is computed on this figure.
Values are in JPY millions, converted from Komatsu's printed JPY billions with 1 decimal (e.g. ¥594.2bn = 594,200).

No YTD derivation was needed: Komatsu prints single 3-month figures, both in its 3-month segment tables and in the appendix chart 'Construction, Mining & Utility Equipment: Quarterly Sales and Segment Profit'. Every quarter is taken from the latest deck whose chart covers it (FY2026 Q2 deck for FY23/1Q–FY26/2Q, FY2025 Q4 deck for FY22, FY2024 Q4 deck for FY21, FY2023 Q4 deck for FY20/4Q).

Restatement (minor, latest figures used): from the FY2022 decks onward, Komatsu shows slightly revised CMU figures for earlier quarters versus the originals. FY21 quarterly sales went from 594.3/591.0/660.1/718.8 to 594.3/591.0/660.2/718.9, FY21 segment profit from 53.6/64.9/73.2/83.8 to 53.7/65.0/73.3/83.9, and FY20/4Q sales from 594.1 to 594.2 (¥bn).
Next report date: Komatsu's IR calendar gives only 'Late Jan, 2027' for the FY2026 Q3 results (no exact day), so next_report_date is null.

FX: the Riksbank publishes the JPY rate as SEK per 100 JPY; fx_rate_to_sek is per 1 JPY (Riksbank SWEA series SEKJPYPMI quarterly average, equal to the per-100 quote / 100; e.g. 2026Q3 6.0598 SEK per 100 JPY = 0.060598 SEK per JPY).

points: CMU sales rose 15.1% year on year to ¥1,032.6 billion in Jul–Sep 2026 (FY2026 Q2) on a weaker yen, higher volume and better selling prices.

CMU segment profit fell 4.5% to ¥114.3 billion and the segment profit ratio dropped to 11.1% as rising costs outweighed the positive effects of the weaker yen, higher volume and better selling prices.

Komatsu raised its FY2026 mining-equipment demand projection to 0% to −5% (from −5% to −10% in July) after Q2 demand grew 5%, with copper and gold mining in Latin America and Africa solid while coal in Asia stayed weak.
